```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(transmap)
data(transmap_example)
Y <- transmap_example$Y
hs <- r_hotspot(Y, min_gene = 5)
```

`transmap_local()` summarizes the expression of each gene module into one or
more program phenotypes. Four constructors are available:

| `method` | Phenotypes per module | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `"WPC"` (default) | All whitened components with eigenvalue > 1 | `null_z` |
| `"PC1"` | First principal component | - |
| `"aPC"` | Adaptive number of principal components | - |
| `"AUCell"` | AUCell enrichment score | Bioconductor `AUCell` |

# 1. Whitened principal components (WPC)

### Why whitening

Genes in a module are correlated for reasons unrelated to the *trans* effect
being mapped: shared regulation by many small effects, technical factors and
cell-type composition. Write the expression covariance of a module as

$$\Sigma_Y = \Sigma_{\text{genetic}} + \Sigma_{\text{noise}}.$$

WPC looks for gene weights $w$ that maximize expression variance relative to
the correlation expected without genetic effects, $R_{\text{noise}}$:

$$\max_w \frac{w^\top \Sigma_Y w}{w^\top R_{\text{noise}} w}.$$

This is solved by whitening the standardized expression by
$R_{\text{noise}}^{-1/2}$ and taking principal components. A component with
eigenvalue above 1 carries more variance than the null correlation explains,
and all such components are kept.

### Estimating the null correlation

$R_{\text{noise}}$ is estimated from null *trans* z-scores (`null_z`, variants
$\times$ genes): the correlation across variants whose largest absolute
z-score over the module genes is below 2 (relaxed to 3 if too few remain;
the identity matrix if still too few).

```{r wpc}
wpc <- transmap_local(Y, hs, method = "WPC", null_z = transmap_example$null_z)
dim(wpc$scores)
wpc$summary
```

`summary` reports, per module, the genes given (`n_genes`) and used
(`n_used`), the number of phenotypes kept (`k`), the threshold used to select
null variants and the number of null variants.

```{r wpc-eigen}
round(wpc$eigenvalues, 3)
```

`loadings` holds the gene weights of each component:

```{r wpc-loadings}
round(wpc$loadings[[1]][1:5, ], 3)
```

`null_z` may also be given as a list with element `z`, the format of the null
z-score files used in the TransMap pipeline:

```{r wpc-list}
wpc_list <- transmap_local(Y, hs, null_z = list(z = transmap_example$null_z))
identical(wpc_list$scores, wpc$scores)
```

# 2. First principal component (PC1)

`PC1` keeps the first principal component of the standardized module
expression: one phenotype per module, without null z-scores.

```{r pc1}
pc1 <- transmap_local(Y, hs, method = "PC1")
dim(pc1$scores)
round(pc1$eigenvalues, 2)
```

# 3. Adaptive principal components (aPC)

`aPC` adds components while (i) the cumulative variance of the previous
components is below `max_cumvar` and (ii) the next component explains more
variance than the Marchenko-Pastur bound $(1 + \sqrt{p/n})^2 / p$, where $p$
is the number of genes and $n$ the number of samples.

```{r apc}
apc <- transmap_local(Y, hs, method = "aPC", max_cumvar = 0.8)
apc$summary[, c("module", "n_used", "k")]
```

# 4. AUCell

`AUCell` scores each module by the area under its gene recovery curve, using
gene rankings of the full expression matrix. `auc_max_rank` sets the fraction
of top-ranked genes considered. AUCell breaks ties at random, so set a seed.

```{r aucell, eval = requireNamespace("AUCell", quietly = TRUE)}
set.seed(1)
auc <- transmap_local(Y, hs, method = "AUCell", auc_max_rank = 0.2)
head(round(auc$scores, 3), 3)
```

# 5. Covariates

With `covariates`, covariates and an intercept are regressed out of the
expression before programs are built (and, for AUCell, also out of the
scores). Only samples shared by `Y` and `covariates` are kept.

```{r covariates}
adj <- transmap_local(Y, hs, null_z = transmap_example$null_z,
                      covariates = transmap_example$covariates)
dim(adj$scores)
```

# 6. Modules from other sources

Any named list of gene sets can be used, for example modules from WGCNA or
curated pathways. A single character vector is treated as one module.

```{r custom}
custom <- transmap_local(Y, transmap_example$modules, method = "PC1")
colnames(custom$scores)

one <- transmap_local(Y, paste0("GENE0", 1:9), method = "PC1")
colnames(one$scores)
```

Genes not in `Y` are ignored. A module with a single available gene uses that
gene's expression as its phenotype.

# 7. Comparing constructors

The first phenotype of each constructor captures the shared module signal, so
the constructors agree closely on the leading component (up to sign):

```{r compare}
round(abs(cor(wpc$scores[, "hotspot_module_1_WPC1"],
              pc1$scores[, "hotspot_module_1"])), 3)
```

WPC additionally returns further components whose variance exceeds the null
expectation. Recommendations:

- Use **WPC** (default) when null *trans* z-scores are available. It accounts
  for background gene-gene correlation and keeps every component that exceeds
  it.
- Use **PC1** for a single, simple summary per module.
- Use **aPC** when modules may carry several independent signals but no null
  z-scores are available.
- Use **AUCell** for rank-based enrichment scores that are robust to the scale
  of expression.

The columns of `scores` are the local program phenotypes. See
[Trans-QTL Mapping with Program Phenotypes](Trans_QTL_Mapping_with_Programs.html)
for how to use them.
